text: This lesson creates and populates all four dimension tables this warehouse needs, each following the same pattern: a surrogate IDENTITY key, plus the original source ID kept as an alternate key.

dw.DimProduct's load resolves the flattening join from Lesson 3 exactly once. The LEFT JOINs matter here — some real products have no subcategory at all, and an inner join would silently drop them out of the warehouse.

dw.DimCustomer adds a column that doesn't exist anywhere in AdventureWorks2012: CustomerType, derived once during the load from whether StoreID is populated. Every front-end can now filter on it directly instead of re-deriving the same logic three times.

dw.DimDate is different — there's no table of dates to borrow from, so it's generated with a recursive CTE covering the real order-date range, with MAXRECURSION 0 to clear SQL Server's default row-count cap.
Next lesson loads the fact table itself, adds the foreign-key constraints that were deferred back in Lesson 4, and validates row counts between the source and the warehouse.
